description: Figure 3 presents a comparison of problem distributions based on correctness, specifically examining the results from settings with and without knowledge using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. The figure consists of two pie charts, one representing the “w/ KNOWLEDGE” setting and the other the “w/o KNOWLEDGE” setting. The “w/ KNOWLEDGE” chart has four slices: “easy” (light blue, 44.6%), “medium” (dark blue, 45.9%), “hard” (light orange, 3.2%), and “N+K+” (dark orange, 6.3%). The “w/o KNOWLEDGE” chart also has four slices: “easy” (light blue, 61.5%), “medium” (dark blue, 29.1%), “hard” (light orange, 3.6%), and “N+K+” (dark orange, 5.8%).  Each chart includes a legend identifying the slice labels and corresponding colors. Percentage labels are displayed inside each slice. The slices within each chart appear to be ordered from largest to smallest, visually representing the proportion of problems falling into each correctness category for each knowledge setting.
